faq.q: What are the three timer modes and their defaults?
faq.a: There are three tabs. Stopwatch counts up with lap recording. Countdown lets you set hours/minutes/seconds (default 5 minutes) with quick presets of 1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, and 60 minutes. Interval is a work/rest timer defaulting to 30s work, 10s rest, 8 rounds. Countdown and Interval play a tone and flash the screen when they finish.

faq.q: Does the stopwatch keep accurate time if I switch tabs?
faq.a: Yes. It records a start timestamp with performance.now() and computes elapsed time as the difference from the current clock, rather than adding a fixed amount each tick. So even when a background tab is throttled, the time stays correct. The Interval timer similarly uses clock deadlines and will apply any phase transitions that were skipped during throttling.

faq.q: What's the difference between Lap Time and Split in the lap table?
faq.a: Lap Time is the duration of that single lap measured from the previous lap marker; Split is the cumulative total elapsed at that marker. With more than one lap, the table tags the fastest lap green and the slowest red. You can delete individual laps, and the remaining splits recalculate. Use Export Laps CSV to download them as laps.csv.

faq.q: What's saved between visits, and does it make sound without files?
faq.a: The running stopwatch state and laps are saved under sw_state, and completed stopwatch sessions over one second are kept under sw_history (last 20). Alarms are generated with the Web Audio API using oscillator tones, so no sound files are downloaded. Keyboard shortcuts work only on the Stopwatch tab: Space start/pause, L lap, R reset.
